subject.summary: A local-only, repo-agnostic bash wrapper that drives the OpenAI Codex CLI as a third, independent reviewer. One invocation assembles a packet (persona → driver context → repo guidance manifest → scoped diff → touched-file bodies), runs Codex config-isolated under a read-only sandbox with a pinned JSON output schema, and prints exactly one JSON status line. Eight modes share that machinery: five review gates (plan, bundle, phase-review, prepr, prepr-delta) that emit APPROVE / BLOCK / INFRA_ERROR / OVERFLOW, a snapshot mode (phase-start), and two non-gate siblings — question (advisory GROUNDED grounding of a decision) and investigate (root-cause report bound by a prompt-layer safety contract). Everything it writes lives under ~/.claude/codex-gate/runs; the target repo is only ever read. The design is uniformly fail-closed: a blocker beats the model's own verdict, an over-budget packet never reaches Codex, an inconclusive shard or lens can never be approved over, and a coverage gap refuses approval outright. The fix-loop itself is NOT here — rounds, convergence and the round cap belong to the calling agent.
